polaris: DGF-N4: independent q controls m(q) and GUP decoherence fluctuations
framework: information geometry: Fisher-Rao / Hellinger angle of binary readout
findings: Define q as a normalized Fisher-Rao/Hellinger phase distance rather than a mass label. Let theta=pi*q/2; a binary readout amplitude sin(theta) gives m=m_star*sin(theta), with m_star=2*m_p/pi. This is structurally identical to the DGF-N4 sine map while avoiding the old I=(m/m_p)^2 loop.
math_object: Bernoulli statistical manifold Fisher-Rao geodesic; equivalent qubit Fubini-Study angle.
strangest_prediction: Microgram-scale center-of-mass interference should show a domain boundary near m_star=13.85 microgram rather than smooth survival to 22 microgram. Candidate system: cryogenic levitated optomechanical silica microspheres with masses 12, 14, 16, 20 microgram; measure background-subtracted fringe visibility.
a_objection: If q can only be inferred from mass and has no independent readout or fluctuation, it is only a reparameterization and DGF-N4 fails.
failed_jumps: rate-distortion gave a bounded variable but no natural sine amplitude
quantum error-correction distance was too discrete
mutual information tends to recreate the old I=(m/m_p)^2 route
next_plan: Write q-fluctuation as Fisher-metric random geodesic noise and test whether it can drive a Lindblad kernel independently of mass.
literature_needed: Wootters statistical distance; Fisher-Rao metric; Fubini-Study metric; macroscopic matter-wave interferometry; levitated optomechanics

claims.statement: The DGF-N4 sine mass map can be interpreted as a Fisher-Rao/Hellinger angle amplitude projection.
assumptions: binary phase readout is physically meaningful
mass is a projection of q rather than q's definition

claims.statement: The 14 vs 22 microgram distinction can be phrased as whether q_inv remains real for masses between 13.85 and 21.76 microgram.
assumptions: environmental decoherence can be independently calibrated
real q-domain failure has an observable signature
